submitted.rationale: Highest measured photocurrent was 7.5e-7 A, at Fe 0.39, Ni 0.18, V 0.42. This low-Ni region with Fe roughly equal to V is FeVO4-like and should absorb 2.72 eV light. It beat both the Fe-rich corner and the more V-rich point.

consultations.verdict: Fe2O3 HSE gap 2.77 eV is marginal vs 2.72 eV photons; Fe-V oxide (FeVO4-type, narrower gap) region with low Ni should absorb 455 nm better. Supports measuring Fe~V, low-Ni candidate 62.

Fe2O3 gap predictions are fidelity-dependent (SCAN 0.81, HSE 2.77); experimentally hematite ~2.1 eV absorbs 455 nm. Model is weakly supportive / largely uninformative; measuring Fe-rich corner 159 to contrast with Fe~V point 62.

Band-gap predictions for Fe2O3 are too inconsistent across fidelities to rank compositions, so I'm treating them as uninformative. The data do point somewhere: 62 (V 0.42) beat 159 (V 0.20), so I'm pushing further toward FeVO4 stoichiometry with low Ni by measuring 90 (Fe 0.34, Ni 0.17, V 0.48).
